thread.title: Watch And Services Not Enough To Save Apple (Victor Dergunov) - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Brian Bain
title: Watch And Services Not Enough To Save Apple (Victor Dergunov) - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
The story behind the interview: Apple ( AAPL ) stock has lost around one-fourth of its value. How concerned should investors be? According to Victor Dergunov, Apple is still a great company, but the days of amazing growth are over, and Watch and Services are not enough to fill the gap.
For those who prefer to read, my full interview notes are copied below.
Link to Viktor Dergunov's original article: Apple: The Demise Of A Growth Era
Interview notes: Apple has been a favorite for Victor for a decade (since 2006) and he’s still long Apple, but has reduced his position and the stock down over 20% (given up over a one-fourth of value).
The reason for the decline in stock price is that for investors it feels like Apple has reached a pinnacle growth level. iPhone unit sales have been flat for years, but making more money due to higher prices. Thanks to price increases, iPhone revenue has increased 27% year over year. Even so, investors worry they can only increase prices so much as the average selling price already is $800.
Apple has three core products (iPhone, Mac, iPad) but as most know the majority of Apple’s revenues come from iPhone (60%). Additionally, the average selling price for iPad already is going down.
Investors can expect revenues to grow slowly or perhaps even be flat going forward.
Apple is no longer a growth company, the market already is penetrated with its products, and there are a lot of competitors with comparable phones that are cheaper.
What about watch and services? Watch still very small and services are growing but still relatively small. Year-over-year “other revenues” (includes Watch) grew 31% (total revenue of $4.2B for the quarter) and services grew 17% (total revenue of $10B for the quarter). Total revenues for the quarter were $62B. iPhone was $37B.
Victor is looking at around 4% revenue growth going forward for Apple.
Another factor weighing on Apple is higher costs due to trade war concerns and tariffs.
Another concern is the potential for a slowdown of the economy in the US and the world. A recession in next year or two will weigh on the iPhone.
Steve Jobs pioneered all the great products for Apple and he’s no longer here.
Apple makes the best of the best products and has a great ecosystem they will continue to monetize and grow.
Longer term Apple will continue to make a lot of money and do great, but the stock will likely struggle or underperform for some time.
